thumbnail_brief: A cross-section with a thin strip of grey, dead conifers on top and a huge white web of bootlace fungus filling the lower two thirds and running out of every edge, tiny red-capped Doug in a Douglas-fir costume standing on top, and the words ALL ONE THING, so the title says what it does (killing trees for 2,400 years) and the thumbnail shows the twist that the whole hidden web is a single organism (no FUNGUS, OREGON, TREES, KILLING or YEARS on the image; no rot or decay on Doug, no cute mushroom faces).
description:
The biggest fungus ever found is a single honey fungus in Oregon's Malheur National Forest: about 965 hectares, at least 2,400 years old, and killing conifers from the roots up while almost all of it stays hidden. Doug works up to it through the giant things that live inside something else or under the ground: the corpse flower, dodder, a ten-meter tapeworm, a tree that cuts cables, Pando and the humongous fungus.

Which one would you least like to stand on? Tell us in the comments.
Subscribe so you don't miss Doug's next bad decision.
